Routes are managed as files in `src/routes`.\n137: \n138: ### Adding A Route\n139: \n140: To add a new route to your application just add a new file in the `./src/routes` directory.\n141: \n142: TanStack will automatically generate the content of the route file for you.\n143: \n144: Now that you have two routes you can use a `Link` component to navigate between them.\n145: \n146: ### Adding Links\n147: \n148: To use SPA (Single Page Application) navigation you will need to import the `Link` component from `@tanstack/react-router`.\n149: \n150: ```tsx\n151: import { Link } from \"@tanstack/react-router\";\n152: ```\n153: \n154: Then anywhere in your JSX you can use it like so:\n155: \n156: ```tsx\n157: <Link to=\"/about\">About</Link>\n158: ```\n159: \n160: This will create a link that will navigate to the `/about` route.\n161: \n162: More information on the `Link` component can be found in the [Link documentation](https://tanstack.com/router/v1/docs/framework/react/api/router/linkComponent).\n163: \n164: ### Using A Layout\n165: \n166: In the File Based Routing setup the layout is located in `src/routes/__root.tsx`. Anything you add to the root route will appear in all the routes. The route content will appear in the JSX where you render `{children}` in the `shellComponent`.\n167: \n168: Here is an example layout that includes a header:\n169: \n170: ```tsx\n171: import { HeadContent, Scripts, createRootRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'\n172: \n173: export const Route = createRootRoute({\n174:   head: () => ({\n175:     meta: [\n176:       { charSet: 'utf-8' },\n177:       { name: 'viewport', content: 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1' },\n178:       { title: 'My App' },\n179:     ],\n180:   }),\n181:   shellComponent: ({ children }) => (\n182:     <html lang=\"en\">\n183:       <head>\n184:         <HeadContent />\n185:       </head>\n186:       <body>\n187:         <header>\n188:           <nav>\n189:             <Link to=\"/\">Home</Link>\n190:             <Link to=\"/about\">About</Link>\n191:           </nav>\n192:         </header>\n193:         {children}\n194:         <Scripts />\n195:       </body>\n196:     </html>\n197:   ),\n198: })\n199: ```\n200: \n201: More information on layouts can be found in the [Layouts documentation](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/routing-concepts#layouts).\n202: \n203: ## Server Functions\n204: \n205: TanStack Start provides server functions that allow you to write server-side code that seamlessly integrates with your client components.\n206: \n207: ```tsx\n208: import { createServerFn } from '@tanstack/react-start'\n209: \n210: const getServerTime = createServerFn({\n211:   method: 'GET',\n212: }).handler(async () => {\n213:   return new Date().toISOString()\n214: })\n215: \n216: // Use in a component\n217: function MyComponent() {\n218:   const [time, setTime] = useState('')\n219:   \n220:   useEffect(() => {\n221:     getServerTime().then(setTime)\n222:   }, [])\n223:   \n224:   return <div>Server time: {time}</div>\n225: }\n226: ```\n227: \n228: ## API Routes\n229: \n230: You can create API routes by using the `server` property in your route definitions:\n231: \n232: ```tsx\n233: import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'\n234: import { json } from '@tanstack/react-start'\n235: \n236: export const Route = createFileRoute('/api/hello')({\n237:   server: {\n238:     handlers: {\n239:       GET: () => json({ message: 'Hello, World!' }),\n240:     },\n241:   },\n242: })\n243: ```\n244: \n245: ## Data Fetching\n246: \n247: There are multiple ways to fetch data in your application. You can use TanStack Query to fetch data from a server. But you can also use the `loader` functionality built into TanStack Router to load the data for a route before it's rendered.\n248: \n249: For example:\n250: \n251: ```tsx\n252: import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'\n253: \n254: export const Route = createFileRoute('/people')({\n255:   loader: async () => {\n256:     const response = await fetch('https://swapi.dev/api/people')\n257:     return response.json()\n258:   },\n259:   component: PeopleComponent,\n260: })\n261: \n262: function PeopleComponent() {\n263:   const data = Route.useLoaderData()\n264:   return (\n265:     <ul>\n266:       {data.results.map((person) => (\n267:         <li key={person.name}>{person.name}</li>\n268:       ))}\n269:     </ul>\n270:   )\n271: }\n272: ```\n273: \n274: Loaders simplify your data fetching logic dramatically.
